analysis.title: Global Rates Trader: Risk Off Inflation
key_insights: GS keeps a constructive tilt on US duration and continues to favor receiving 10s on the 5s10s30s SOFR fly. Yields are still on the high side of fair value, and the bank's bond fund positioning estimate is at levels typically followed by lower yields over the next quarters.

US yields fell as pressure in AI-related equities and pockets of credit outweighed firmer-than-expected September inflation data. Bonds have been a poor hedge for broad equity indices amid energy volatility but a better diversifier for the AI theme (Exhibit 1).

Recent inflation news keeps broader hike risks sticky, though Fed officials' comments indicate the FOMC is set to pause in October. Front-end rallies are likely constrained near term, so GS prefers longs in the 10y part of the curve.

UST absorption has been smooth despite weak appetite during the early autumn selloff. Banks added about $40bn USTs net since late summer, money market funds were another source of demand, and Treasury exhausted the full $6bn buyback envelope. GS sees a collective effort rather than any outsized investor base.

The US 3y swap spread has underperformed modestly while front-end and belly spreads are near GS fair value and the long end remains wide to fundamentals. GS sees risk to long-end spread outperformance into the Treasury refunding if auction sizes stay steady or buybacks change only a little, so it prefers expressing spread longs in the 3y sector.

Repo rates have stayed at or below IORB, and the Fed has kept reserve management purchases at zero for three straight months. GS expects zero balance sheet expansion could extend into next year, with a high hurdle to outright balance sheet reduction.

Two consecutive weak Canadian labor reports lowered BoC hike pricing to 8bp for October. CAD rates trade in lockstep with US rates outside domestic data days, and GS sees risk/reward favoring 2s5s flatteners or paying October BoC tactically into CPI. GS expects CAD rates to benefit most if the US rally extends.

In the Euro area, ECB communication is cautious. Pricing is on the hawkish side of GS economists' base case of one more hike in December, and energy upside would mainly front-load hike risk into Q1 2027.

OAT spreads continue to stabilize, but the budget bill is unlikely to be resolved before mid-December. OAT-Bund spreads are wide of fundamentals and above the 100bp stressed level GS expected into the elections, so there is scope for tightening if core rates offer relief, though conviction on the landing zone is low.

GS expects Bund support to persist. Rising sovereign stress has historically coincided with lower Bund yields, Italian political risk premium is contained, and markets may be unwilling to price both high Bund yields and wide sovereign spreads. Front-end vs belly flatteners such as 2s5s offer better protection against energy upside.

Gilts have been resilient despite the highest sensitivity to energy among G10 markets. GS economists' baseline is one November BoE hike, and better Gilt performance needs easing of energy and fiscal headwinds, with upside risk to European gas if LNG flows through Hormuz fail to recover.

JGB long-end pressure has eased, with 2s10s and 5s10s flattening and 10y JGBs outperforming the G4. GS keeps paying 5s on the 2s5s10s fly as protection against renewed tightening risk, citing firm September Tokyo CPI and a possibly dovish October BoJ.

risk_factors: Energy volatility, especially TTF gas and Hormuz LNG flows, could keep hike risk elevated.
Sticky inflation could lift broader hike risks.
The Treasury refunding decision could hurt long-end swap spread outperformance.
French fiscal and political uncertainty may persist, with the budget unresolved until at least mid-December.
Bund supply is a headwind to sustained outperformance.
The UK budget scale and funding of cost-of-living measures are a risk to Gilts.
A reversal of the US-led rally could expose CAD rates.
A dovish October BoJ or more front-loaded Fed tightening could pressure JGB belly rates.
charts_described: Exhibit 8 plots 10y bond total returns since January 1, 2026 against 2y1y sensitivity to oil, showing Gilts relatively close to the developed markets average despite high energy sensitivity.
Exhibit 9 shows cumulative change in G4 10y yields since 1 September, with 10y JGBs outperforming the rest of the G4.
vol_and_positioning: GS fund positioning indicator is at a more pronounced underweight (current score -2), consistent with lower yields over subsequent quarters.
The option implied position indicator is at 1 and the US Data Response Indicator is at 0.
CFTC duration-weighted positioning: Spec net -76.8 in SFR and -49.9 in TY. Leveraged funds are -127.8 in TY, asset managers +161.7 in TY, and dealers -35.8 in TY.
Reduced net longs in UST futures may reflect asset managers shifting into cash bonds because of CTD switch risk.
Dealer inventories are diminished, consistent with orderly absorption amid a compressed basis opportunity set.
Average daily SOFR volumes over the last three months are about $200bn lower than Q4 of last year.
geopolitical: Euro area sovereign stress, particularly French fiscal and election risk, is feeding lower Bund yields.
LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz have not fully recovered, posing upside risk to European gas prices.
The start of the war in Iran is cited as a past episode of fleeting Bund outperformance.
Renewed trade tensions are cited as a reason the BoC stays on hold.

tension_points.bull_case: Yields sit above fair value, fund positioning is underweight, and duration has diversified AI-related equity risk, which supports longs in the 10y.
tension_points.bear_case: Inflation data keeps hike risk sticky, energy volatility has made USTs a poor broad equity hedge, and front-end rallies are constrained.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The 5s10s30s fly reaching the 0.04 stop level.

tension_points.bull_case: Front-end sovereign credit curves are tightening, and OAT-Bund spreads are wide of fundamentals, leaving scope for compression.
tension_points.bear_case: There is little follow-through at the 10y point, fiscal risk persists, and the budget is unresolved until at least mid-December.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Compression depends on benign core rate relief or lower core rates volatility, so higher core rates volatility would undercut it.

tension_points.bull_case: Gilt returns have been resilient despite high energy sensitivity, and the supply and QT profile is supportive.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy risk, upside risk to European gas prices, and the budget remain headwinds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz failing to recover further.
